knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: In-place mutation of autograd hook-produced views conflicts with gradient graph bookkeeping
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: When autograd wraps outputs through hooks, subsequent in-place operations on those outputs can create view-mutation cases that the autograd engine rejects or mishandles because the mutation would override the custom backward association.

risk_dimensions.memory: Aliased or view-based storage shared between forward output and in-place mutation path
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Autograd enabled; full backward hooks registered; hooked output consumed by an in-place operation

failure_mechanism.description: The autograd graph records a view produced inside a backward hook wrapper. An in-place modification of that view conflicts with the custom backward logic because handling view and in-place mutation together would override or invalidate the hook-associated backward function.

input_exploration: Build module graphs where a backward hook is registered on one module and its output is passed through operations that may mutate inputs in place
Vary the in-place operation types to include activation, normalization, and elementwise operations that offer in-place execution modes
Use input tensors that require gradients so autograd view tracking remains active
Test both simple and nested module structures to expose graph-state interactions
constraint_awareness: Backward hook registration changes the autograd node and output wrapper type
In-place operations on view outputs require autograd to reconcile view tracking with mutation
Gradient mode must remain enabled for the conflict to appear
oracle_strategy: Monitor for runtime errors reporting that a view created inside a custom Function or backward hook is being modified in place
Detect messages indicating that in-place view modification would override custom backward logic
Treat such exceptions as contract violations even when no numerical mismatch occurs

transferability.reason: The conflict arises from general autograd graph invariants involving backward hooks, view tracking, and in-place mutation, so it can apply to any differentiable API that exposes hooks and in-place operations, not only the original activation API.

llm_reasoning_guidance.important_considerations: Focus on combinations of autograd state changes, such as full backward hooks, with operations that mutate their inputs. Vary module types, hook placement, and in-place operation categories rather than fixing a single activation function.
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that compose backward hooks with in-place operations on forward outputs under gradient mode. Let the framework track views and mutations, and use exception or oracle checks to detect autograd contract violations. Avoid hard-coding the original API-specific reproduction and instead explore the underlying hook plus in-place mutation pattern.
